cards.hook: Planning to upgrade? Build your next deposit inside an offset.
cards.so_what: Own an investment? Ask whether an offset on that loan should hold your savings. Tax side with your accountant.

posts.linkedin:
Planning to upgrade? Build your next deposit inside an offset.

If you already own an investment property and want to buy your next home, here's a setup we like. Keep the investment loan interest-only, attach an offset to it, and build that offset hard.

While the money sits there, it cuts the interest on the investment loan. When you buy, it comes out and becomes a bigger deposit on the new home. That keeps the loan on the place you live in smaller, and that's the interest you can't claim.

How the tax side works for you is one for your accountant.

If upgrading is on the cards, ask where your savings should live until then.

General information only, not personal advice.

cards.hook: Building with a mate? Don’t do it in your own names.
cards.so_what: Ask your accountant about a trust or company before you sign anything together.

posts.linkedin:
Building with a mate? Don't do it in your own names.

Two friends, a block of land, a plan for a couple of townhouses. It's a common way people get into their first project. The part that gets skipped is whose name it all goes in.

We'd recommend a trust or company structure, set up with your accountant, rather than your individual names. Two reasons.

It limits how far a problem with the project can reach into your personal finances. And two strong borrowers pooled in one structure can support a bigger project with mainstream lenders than either could alone.

Get the structure sorted with your accountant before you sign anything together.

General information only, not personal advice.

#propertydevelopment #jointventure #smallbusiness

cards.text:
Your current bank can often do what you need.

Need a top-up, or more for the build? Most people assume that means moving the whole loan.

Moving costs you: discharge fees, switching costs, a new application from scratch.

So we ask your lender first. We switch when the rate or structure is meaningfully better elsewhere. Not just to move it.

posts.linkedin:
Your current bank can often do what you need. Ask them first.

When someone needs a top-up, or more money for a renovation or build, the assumption is often that the whole loan has to move. Sometimes it should. Often it doesn't.

Moving has a cost: discharge fees, switching costs, and a fresh application. Where your lender can do the variation, staying put is usually the easier path.

So that's where we start. We ask the existing lender first, and we only switch if the rate or structure is meaningfully better somewhere else.

Before you refinance to get a top-up, ask whether a variation with your current lender gets the same result.

General information only, not personal advice.

#refinance #homeloan

cards.body: A 15-minute chat is enough to know where you stand.

posts.linkedin:
Don't buy a brand-new apartment just to get the grant.

The first home owner grant is real money, and it's tempting to shop for a property that qualifies. Our view: don't let it pick the property for you. New apartments are often priced high for what they are, and if you overpay by more than the grant, you've gone backwards.

What we quietly like instead: older, smaller unit blocks. Ten to fifteen one- or two-bedroom units on a decent-sized block, no lift. Body corporate costs stay low, and the land underneath has appeal down the track. They take some finding, but they tend to hold their value.

Before a view sells you, ask why the body corporate fees are what they are.

General information only, not personal advice.

#firsthomebuyer #firsthome #melbourneproperty
